slides.subline: HOW THEY FOUND OUT IS EVEN WORSE

slides.headline: AMAZON'S AI WENT 860% OVER BUDGET
slides.body: Amazon asked an AI called Claude to handle a single coding job. The final bill: $1.8 million. That's 860% more than they planned to spend

slides.headline: THEY CALLED THE TASK 'MENIAL'
slides.body: Amazon's own team described the coding job as 'menial', meaning basic everyday work. They later called the bill 'catastrophically expensive' in their internal reports

slides.headline: NOBODY NOTICED UNTIL THEY CHECKED
slides.body: The $1.8 million wasn't caught by a person or an alert system. Amazon only discovered it when someone pulled up their internal AI spending numbers, and by then the money was already gone

slides.headline: MOST BUSINESSES NEVER CHECK THEIR AI BILLS
slides.body: If Amazon, one of the biggest companies on earth, burned $1.8 million on AI without catching it, smaller businesses don't stand a chance. A single audit of your AI spending catches the waste in under an hour

slides.headline: THIS WON'T BE THE LAST TIME
slides.body: Every company is rushing to use AI, and most have zero guardrails on what it costs. Follow, you'll want to see who's next. Send this to the friend whose company just started throwing AI at everything

caption:
Swipe to see how Amazon accidentally burned $1.8 million on one AI coding task 💸

Amazon used Claude, an AI coding tool, to handle one task and it cost $1.8 million, 860% over budget. Their own team called the work 'menial.' Amazon's internal report described the bill as 'catastrophically expensive.' Nobody caught it until someone checked the AI usage numbers.

Companies are throwing AI at everything but almost nobody tracks what it costs. If Amazon missed a $1.8 million mistake, most businesses don't stand a chance.
